- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–15% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >40% from prior 7-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +10–15% above immediate prior value.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 40), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 3-day moving average of true values.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (e.g., -0.3 to 0.3), model often overconfidently predicts upward trend; reduce forecast slope by 20–30%.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after high sentiment (e.g., -0.7 followed by 3-day low), model often fails to anticipate; add 1–2 day lag correction.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in cycle (first 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 3–8% for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- If sentiment turns positive after negative streak (e.g., -0.7 → +0.3), model often underreacts; increase forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
